about.title: Montclair Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Montclair sits at a busy crossing point of San Bernardino County commerce, with warehouses, distribution centers, and retail operations lining Central Avenue, Monte Vista Avenue, and the corridors near I-10. Workers in these settings face forklift accidents, loading dock injuries, and vehicle-related incidents, especially with area traffic peaking Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. In California, workers' compensation usually covers injuries sustained on the job, but that system pays medical costs and a portion of lost wages, not full compensation for pain and suffering. When a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp case. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise results, but we can connect injured Montclair workers with an independent attorney who understands both systems, so you can find out what options actually exist in your situation without cost or obligation on your part.

whyChoose.title: Why Injured Montclair Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California treats workers' comp as the usual exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be held liable separately.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and missing that window can complicate your claim, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report injuries or file claims, and an attorney can help you understand your protections if that becomes a concern.

items.question: I was hurt at a warehouse job near I-10 in Montclair. Do I only have a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Workers' comp usually applies against your direct employer, but if a third party like a delivery contractor, equipment manufacturer, or property owner contributed to the accident, you may have a separate claim. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your Montclair workplace incident to see what applies.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer?
items.answer: California generally requires you to report a workplace injury within 30 days. Waiting longer can create problems with your claim, so it's best to report as soon as you're able and seek medical attention promptly.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: No, retaliation against an employee for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you're facing retaliation after an injury near Central Avenue or elsewhere in Montclair, an attorney can help you understand your rights.
